audit_title: CRISPR Guide AI: Cross-Cell-Line Transfer & Sequence Overlap Audit
description: Quantifies exact guide sequence sharing between cell line datasets arising from common screening libraries (Toronto KnockOut v1 library from Hart et al. 2015). Reclassifies cross-cell evaluation as cross-cell transfer rather than independent external validation, and decomposes transfer into seen vs unseen guide sequences.

HeLa_vs_HCT116.screening_library_provenance: Toronto KnockOut (TKO) v1 library (Hart et al. 2015)

HeLa_vs_HL60.screening_library_provenance: Distinct libraries (TKO v1 vs Wang et al. 2014 ribosomal library)

HeLa_vs_A375.screening_library_provenance: Completely disjoint (Genome-wide dropout vs Doench 2016 8-gene tiling)

subset_seen_in_source_training_dev_pool.category_label: Guide sequences observed in source training set (HeLa dev pool)
subset_seen_in_source_training_dev_pool.interpretation: Strong correlation driven by sequence memorization/re-encounter across cell lines.

subset_not_seen_in_source_training_dev_p.category_label: Guide sequences not observed in source training set (HeLa dev pool)
subset_not_seen_in_source_training_dev_p.interpretation: True generalization correlation on novel guide sequences without sequence memorization.

subset_seen_in_source_training_dev_pool.category_label: Guide sequences observed in source training set (HCT116 dev pool)

subset_not_seen_in_source_training_dev_p.category_label: Guide sequences not observed in source training set (HCT116 dev pool)

scientific_cautions: Unseen guide sequences do NOT necessarily represent unseen genes; many belong to the same core essential gene set screened in TKO v1.
Cross-cell transfer MUST NOT be described as independent external validation.
The apparent cross-cell transfer correlation (r = 0.4069) is predominantly driven by the 78.66% seen guide sequences (r = 0.4470); novel unseen sequences achieve r = 0.2470.
